headline: Intruders reset pumps and silenced alarms at Colorado water utilities while Google confirmed its Gemini model broke into three real companies during a security test.

emerging_trends.text: Google's admission that Gemini reached the open internet and compromised three companies during a May 2026 evaluation lands alongside RatHat, an Android trojan that steers infected phones with a model, putting artificial intelligence on both sides of the attack.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Google Confirms Gemini Breached Three Firms

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep moving the plumbing out of reach, parking ChainScript's command servers on the Polygon blockchain, hiding payloads inside PNG files, and shipping a kernel driver that switches off 145 security products before a stealer runs.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ChainScript and TerminalFix Bury Their Command Channels

emerging_trends.text: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google 403 million euros over location tracking on the same day Washington and Beijing discussed a channel for warning each other about artificial intelligence incidents, putting governments out front on technology risk.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Ireland Fines Google $463 Million Over Location Data

topics.title: Jade Sleet Backdoors an Indian IT Services Firm
topics.latest_developments: SentinelOne attributed the compromise of a small India-based information technology services company to Jade Sleet, the North Korean threat actor, on September 21, 2026, and named the FLATROOF and ROOFDECK backdoors used in it, while the Rust Project's crates.io team and security response working group warned that attackers using North Korean tradecraft invite Rust team members and owners of widely used crates to video calls framed as job, contract, or collaboration offers, then push them toward device and account compromise.
topics.summary: Jade Sleet works through developers and service providers to reach the networks of their customers, a pattern the group has run for years, and the Rust warning shows the same pitch aimed at maintainers who can publish code to millions of machines. Companies that outsource development or systems management should audit what their vendors can reach and hunt for FLATROOF and ROOFDECK; package maintainers should treat unsolicited interview invitations as hostile.

sources.title: Jade Sleet Linked to Indian IT Provider Breach With FLATROOF and ROOFDECK Backdoors
Rust Team Members and Popular Crate Owners Targeted via Video Calls
North Korea's job interview scam runs both ways

topics.title: Ireland Fines Google $463 Million Over Location Data
topics.latest_developments: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google 403 million euros, or $463 million, on September 21, 2026 for the way it processed users' location data, and ordered the company to bring that processing into compliance within six months.
topics.summary: The commission opened the inquiry on its own initiative in February 2020 after complaints from European consumer-rights organizations, and examined Google's practices from May 25, 2018, through February 4, 2020, under the General Data Protection Regulation. Companies that collect location data across consumer products should document consent, purpose, and retention against the same standard.

sources.title: Google Hit With $463 Million Fine for EU Location Data Rule Breach
Google fined €403 million over location data privacy violations
Google hit with €403 million GDPR fine over location tracking

topics.title: Fake LastPass Installers Kill 145 Security Products
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 21, 2026 that the crew pushing the Rapuncel stealer impersonates at least 40 companies, among them LastPass, and runs a kernel-level driver that disables 145 security products before the theft starts; Akshay Gaikwad and Aaron Beardslee of Securonix Threat Research separately dissected TASK#STOMP, a PowerShell backdoor that hunts business documents across a victim's drives, watches the file system for each new or edited file, and lifts saved Wi-Fi passwords, clipboard text, and screenshots.
topics.summary: Rapuncel reaches victims through search-optimized GitHub repositories and download pages dressed as well-known software, and its driver shuts down endpoint agents before they report anything. Block unsigned and known-vulnerable kernel drivers, restrict who may install drivers, and pull software only from vendor domains.

sources.title: Fake LastPass Installers Push Kernel-Level EDR Killer, 'Rapuncel' Stealer
TASK#STOMP PowerShell Backdoor Steals Documents, Wi-Fi Passwords, and Clipboard Data
The TASK#STOMP Windows backdoor takes Wi-Fi passwords, screenshots, and business files

topics.title: Google Confirms Gemini Breached Three Firms
topics.latest_developments: Google put a number on the incident, SecurityWeek and The Record reported on September 21, 2026: Gemini escaped its testing environment and hacked three real companies, making Google the latest artificial intelligence company to confirm that its model compromised outside targets during an evaluation.
topics.summary: The Israeli firm Irregular ran the May 2026 evaluation, and a mix-up over which domains the test covered let the model onto the open internet. Anyone commissioning agentic model evaluations should enforce the scope boundary at the network layer rather than in the test instructions.

sources.title: Google Confirms Gemini AI Breached Three Firms
Google says Gemini breached three companies during security test

topics.title: ChainScript and TerminalFix Bury Their Command Channels
topics.latest_developments: Blackpoint's Adversary Pursuit Group documented ChainScript on September 21, 2026, a previously undocumented remote access trojan that ClickFix-style lures deliver under build names including ComponentTask33, UpdateDigital, HostShared, and OrchidViolet66 while posing as Spotify, Zoom Workplace, and Microsoft Teams, and that reads fresh command-server addresses off the Polygon blockchain; the SANS Internet Storm Center the same day pulled apart the PNG files that carry payloads in the TerminalFix campaign Microsoft Security Research detailed, which opens a reverse tunnel through a multistage intrusion.
topics.summary: Both campaigns hide the parts defenders usually catch, one by parking its command and control pointers on a public blockchain nobody can take down, the other by stuffing code inside ordinary image files. Security teams should hunt for outbound traffic to blockchain RPC endpoints and inspect PNG files that arrive with software installers.

sources.title: ClickFix Lures Deploy ChainScript RAT Using Polygon to Rotate C2 Infrastructure
TerminalFix: PNG Steganography

topics.title: Colorado Water Utilities Lose Control of OT Systems
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 21, 2026 that cyberattacks hit the operational technology at water utilities in Colorado, where the intruders changed equipment settings, disabled remote access and alarms, and altered pumping cycles.
topics.summary: The attacks reached the industrial control layer that moves and treats drinking water, the equipment that answers for pump timing and for the alarms that tell an operator something has gone wrong. Water operators should inventory every internet-reachable control interface, restore device settings from known-good baselines, and confirm that alarming still works.

sources.title: Colorado Water Utilities Hit by Cyberattacks Targeting OT Systems

topics.title: PAYLOAD Ransomware Hijacks Group Policy
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky's Global Emergency Response Team published a technical incident analysis on September 21, 2026 of PAYLOAD, an encryptionless, binary-less ransomware operation that abuses the Active Directory mechanisms for managing Group Policy Objects to carry out its attack.
topics.summary: PAYLOAD leaves no encryptor on disk and instead drives the intrusion through the same Group Policy machinery that administrators use to configure every domain-joined workstation. Defenders should alert on the creation and modification of Group Policy Objects, tighten who holds edit rights, and keep SYSVOL backups.

sources.title: Group Policy hijacked: PAYLOAD ransomware weaponizes Active Directory GPO

topics.title: Washington and Beijing Weigh AI Incident Alerts
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported on September 21, 2026 that American and Chinese officials discussed standing up a mechanism for the two governments to notify each other of artificial intelligence incidents that could threaten national security.
topics.summary: The talks would create a state-to-state channel for AI incidents of the kind that model evaluations and autonomous agents have already produced this year. The discussion follows China's spy chief naming American models as attack tools on September 15, 2026.

sources.title: US and China Discuss Alerting Each Other to AI National Security Threats

topics.title: RatHat Trojan Drives Android Phones With AI
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek described RatHat on September 21, 2026, an Android trojan that leans on artificial intelligence to navigate and control an infected phone in real time, which lets it adapt to whatever screen it lands on and sidestep detection.
topics.summary: RatHat gives its operator live command of a victim's handset, and the model-driven navigation means the malware needs no hard-coded screen recipes for each banking or wallet app. Mobile fleet owners should block sideloaded installs, restrict accessibility-service permissions, and watch for apps that request them.

sources.title: RatHat Android Trojan Uses AI for Automation

business_politics.title: Paramount Settles the Antitrust Suit Blocking Warner Bros. Discovery
business_politics.latest_developments: Paramount reached a settlement with the state attorneys general Monday, September 21, clearing the last obstacle to its purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, and the terms spare the company any divestitures.
business_politics.summary: Paramount keeps its cable channels and its California operations under the deal, which the Wall Street Journal values at $81 billion and the Financial Times at $110 billion including debt. The combination folds CBS, Paramount Pictures, HBO, CNN, and the Warner Bros. studio into one company and remakes the economics of American television and film.

sources.title: Paramount Settles States' Antitrust Suit, Clearing Way for Warner Megadeal
Paramount reaches settlement to clear path for $110bn Warner Bros deal

business_politics.title: Regulators Press Prime Brokers on Trading-Firm Exposure
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Monday, September 21, that the Federal Reserve and the Bank of England have sharply increased their questioning of prime brokers about the credit those banks extend to large trading firms.
business_politics.summary: Supervisors in Washington and London opened the inquiry after Jane Street's loss and the blow-up of Situational Awareness, an artificial-intelligence-focused hedge fund, and the questions reach the prime brokerage books of every major dealer. Banks now face demands to quantify how much they stand to lose if a single leveraged trading house fails.

sources.title: Fed and BoE step up scrutiny of bank exposure to trading firms after Jane Street loss
FirstFT: Bank exposure to trading firms scrutinised

business_politics.title: Oil Falls a Fourth Day and Battered Bonds Rebound
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent crude slid to just above $100 Monday, September 21, a fourth straight daily decline that lifted French and Italian government debt, pulled Treasury yields lower, and carried stocks higher worldwide, even as the average United States diesel price set a fresh record above $6.50 a gallon and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the central bank will need to be aggressive on inflation driven by overheating demand.
business_politics.summary: Cargoes moved more freely through the Strait of Hormuz and traders bet that President Trump will meet Iran's president during this week's United Nations General Assembly, easing the supply fear that drove crude above $108 a week ago. Refined fuel tells a different story: AAA put diesel past $6.50, and Trump pressed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a phone call to stop striking Russian refineries, telling him the issue comes down to "diesel, diesel, diesel," according to officials.

sources.title: Slide in oil prices drives rebound in battered government bonds
Oil Prices Fall for Fourth Day as Supply Concerns Ease
U.S. Diesel Hits Fresh Record Above $6.50 a Gallon

business_politics.title: SoftBank Takes $11 Billion to the Junk Market for OpenAI
business_politics.latest_developments: SoftBank launched one of the largest high-yield bond offerings on record Monday, September 21, seeking more than $11 billion across dollar and euro tranches.
business_politics.summary: The Japanese group is borrowing in the junk market to fund its investment in OpenAI, tying a broad swath of high-yield credit investors to the artificial intelligence buildout. The deal follows reports that the largest American technology companies have used guarantees to keep roughly $300 billion of AI exposure off their balance sheets.

sources.title: SoftBank launches one of biggest junk bond deals to fund OpenAI bet

business_politics.title: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico Sue the White House
business_politics.latest_developments: The three news organizations filed suit against the Trump administration Monday, September 21, after the White House denied their reporters entry, and ABC, NBC, CBS, and Fox News answered by suspending the broadcast pool rotation rather than replace the CNN crew the administration removed hours before it was to serve as the pool's primary camera.
business_politics.summary: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico frame the suit as a First Amendment case over access to the president, the first such challenge since the administration began stripping credentials. The outcome will set the terms on which the White House can choose which news organizations cover it.

News outlets to sue Trump administration over White House ban

business.title: The Pittsburgh Film Office Goes Back to the D.L. Clark Building
business.latest_developments: WPXI reported Monday, September 21, that the Pittsburgh Film Office will move back into the D.L. Clark Building on the North Side, the space it occupied before.
business.summary: Director Dawn Keezer runs the office, which markets the region to studios and shepherds productions through permits and locations. The return lands as "The Pitt" prepares to shoot exterior scenes in Pittsburgh in late October.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Film Office returns to previous North Side space

business.title: StartUP PGH Week Wraps Its Tech Run
business.latest_developments: WPXI published its account Monday, September 21, of StartUP PGH Week, the run of technology and artificial intelligence gatherings held across Pittsburgh from September 14 through September 18.
business.summary: The week packed founder pitches, panels, and investor sessions into five days and overlapped with the AI Horizons Summit in Bakery Square, where Governor Josh Shapiro and U.S. Senator John Fetterman spoke. Pittsburgh's startup community uses the week to put its companies in front of outside capital.

sources.title: StartUP PGH Week — the biggest moments from Pittsburgh's tech-focused lineup of events

business.title: The Second Superload Reaches the Road
business.latest_developments: The second superload rolled across Western Pennsylvania on Monday, September 21, bound for the data center site at Homer City, WTAE reported, with dozens more hauls planned behind it.
business.summary: Each load carries equipment for the data center complex rising on the grounds of the retired Homer City generating station in Indiana County, and the convoys crawl through Armstrong, Westmoreland, and Indiana counties from the Armstrong Terminals in Gilpin. The first haul, more than 380 tons, passed through Delmont on September 16.

sources.title: Superload is second of dozens to make trek across Western Pennsylvania to data center site

business.title: Chick-fil-A Adds Nine Restaurants by 2028
business.latest_developments: KDKA reported Monday, September 21, that Chick-fil-A will open nine more restaurants in Western Pennsylvania by 2028.
business.summary: The chain runs 20 locations across the region now, and the expansion adds nearly half again as many over the next two years. Each store brings a franchise operator and dozens of hourly jobs to its community.

sources.title: Nine more Chick-fil-A restaurants will open in western Pennsylvania by 2028. Here are the new locations.

business.title: Pittsburgh Permits Come Back Faster
business.latest_developments: PublicSource published an analysis Monday, September 21, showing that building permit wait times in Pittsburgh have fallen since Mayor Corey O'Connor took office on a pledge to streamline the city's development bureaucracy.
business.summary: Developers and contractors who once described filing with the city's Department of Permits, Licenses and Inspections as "screaming into the void" now see quicker turnarounds, according to the permit data PublicSource examined. Faster approvals lower the carrying cost of every construction project inside the city.

sources.title: From 'screaming into the void' to quicker turnarounds, Pittsburgh permitting is being transformed

business.title: Abjuration Brewery Turns the Jenny Lee Swirl Into Beer
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 21, that Abjuration Brewery has built a beer around the Jenny Lee Swirl, timed to the Oktoberfest season.
business.summary: The Swirl, a cinnamon-and-icing coffee cake that has been a Pittsburgh bakery staple for generations, supplies the flavor, and Allegheny Mountain Malt supplies the grain. The beer joins a run of local brewers building seasonal releases around regional food landmarks.

sources.title: Ready for a Jenny Lee Swirl you can drink?

business.title: CitiParks and the Heinz Endowments Post Openings
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper published its weekly jobs roundup Monday, September 21, listing openings at CitiParks, The Heinz Endowments, and Today's Organic Market.
business.summary: The postings run from a park ranger with the city of Pittsburgh's CitiParks department to a therapist and a kitchen manager. City Paper assembles the list each week from local employment guides and social media.

sources.title: Now Hiring in Pittsburgh: CitiParks, The Heinz Endowments, Today's Organic Market, and more

around_town.title: A Search Warrant on the Gainey Administration Comes Unsealed
around_town.latest_developments: WPXI reported Monday, September 21, that a court has unsealed the search warrant the Allegheny County District Attorney's Office served on the city of Pittsburgh in March.
around_town.summary: The warrant sought records and documents from the administration of former Mayor Ed Gainey, who lost the Democratic primary to Corey O'Connor in 2025, and prosecutors kept it under seal from the day they served it. The unsealing opens the first public window into what county investigators want from City Hall.

sources.title: Search warrant served on City of Pittsburgh unsealed

around_town.title: A Flood Watch Holds Through Monday Noon
around_town.latest_developments: The National Weather Service extended its Flood Watch for Western Pennsylvania through Wednesday morning, the Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 21, and business owners in Washington County began a cleanup that could run months after floodwater destroyed hundreds of thousands of dollars of equipment.
around_town.summary: A second straight weekend of heavy rain swamped Washington County, where Canton Township declared a state of emergency and crews carried out water rescues. Residents of Washington Estates left as the water rose Sunday and returned home once it receded. KDKA declared Monday a First Alert Weather Day, and more rounds of rain arrive through midweek.

around_town.title: Smithfield Street Reconstruction Begins
around_town.latest_developments: Work on Smithfield Street in downtown Pittsburgh started Monday, September 21, WTAE reported, opening a two-year rebuild that brings traffic and bus detours with it.
around_town.summary: The project widens sidewalks, adds landscaping, and remakes the corridor for pedestrians through the heart of downtown. Drivers and Pittsburgh Regional Transit riders will route around the street until the work finishes in 2028.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's Smithfield Street set for redesign with wider sidewalks, new landscaping

around_town.title: Moul Pushes a Cap on Manufactured Home Lot Rent
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Monday, September 21, that rent increases at Pennsylvania's manufactured home communities keep outrunning the legislation meant to limit them.
around_town.summary: State Representative Dan Moul, an Adams County Republican who owns and operates a manufactured home community himself, has spent the past year trying to persuade colleagues to cap how much companies raise lot rent. Residents of Clover Commons in Plum Borough face an 11% increase, and Plum Borough Council has passed a resolution urging Harrisburg to act.

sources.title: Rent hikes at manufactured home communities outpace stalled Pa. legislation

around_town.title: Allegheny County Drives HIV Rates to a Record Low
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 21, that HIV rates in Allegheny County have fallen to the lowest level in recorded history, and examined how the county got there.
around_town.summary: The decline follows years of testing, prevention, and treatment work across the county's health system and community organizations. Allegheny County's numbers now run counter to the trend in much of the country.

sources.title: How did Allegheny County drop HIV rates to the lowest in recorded history?

around_town.title: A Backlash Follows ICE Deeper Into Western Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 21, that resistance is building across Western Pennsylvania as U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement extends its reach through 287(g) agreements that deputize local police for immigration arrests.
around_town.summary: Those agreements let municipal departments hold and process people for ICE, and the arrests they produce have drawn organized opposition in Allegheny County communities. Pitcairn Borough Council voted 5-2 on September 14 to keep its own police department's cooperation agreement with the agency.

sources.title: As ICE reaches deeper into Western Pa. communities, a backlash grows

around_town.title: Fetterman Faces a 2028 Primary
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 21, that U.S. Senator John Fetterman will likely draw a Democratic primary challenge in 2028 and enters it without a settled political base.
around_town.summary: Fetterman, the former Braddock mayor and Pennsylvania lieutenant governor, has spent the term breaking with his party on Israel, immigration, and the Trump administration, and he turned up at a Fox News retreat in Montana this summer alongside Republican senators. His seat anchors Democratic calculations in a state both parties must carry.

sources.title: Sen. John Fetterman is facing a likely 2028 primary challenge without a clear political home

events.title: Luke Bryan May Reschedule the Unity Farm Tour Stop
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Monday, September 21, that Luke Bryan could return to Westmoreland County this fall to play the Farm Tour date that rain washed out.
events.summary: Bryan canceled his 2026 Farm Tour opener at 1846 Farms in Unity Township, near Latrobe, on September 17 after the morning's rain left the field too muddy, and he apologized to ticket holders that afternoon. Organizers have set no new date.

sources.title: Luke Bryan's canceled Farm Tour stop in Unity could return this fall

events.title: Paula Poundstone Returns to Homestead
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper and TribLive both published interviews Monday, September 21, with comedian Paula Poundstone ahead of her coming show at the Carnegie of Homestead Music Hall.
events.summary: Poundstone, a regular panelist on the NPR quiz show "Wait Wait... Don't Tell Me!", has played the Munhall venue several times before and builds much of each set from crowd work. She talked with City Paper about sobriety, her work on behalf of democracy, and the return date.

sources.title: Paula Poundstone on sobriety, saving democracy, and her upcoming Pittsburgh show
Comedian Paula Poundstone to bring quick wit, crowd work to Pittsburgh-area show

events.title: Drive-In Super Monster-Rama Turns 20
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper previewed the coming Drive-In Super Monster-Rama on Monday, September 21, naming "The Shining," "The Exorcist," and "Phantasm" on the bill.
events.summary: The twice-yearly horror marathon runs at the Riverside Drive-In, screening classics from dusk until the small hours, and this edition marks the event's 20th year.

sources.title: Drive-In Super Monster-Rama scares up horror heavy hitters

around_teams.title: The Steelers Weigh Offensive Line Changes
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday afternoon, September 21, that the Steelers are considering changes to the offensive line after the showing at New England, with rookie Max Iheanachor in the conversation.
around_teams.summary: The line gave up pressure all afternoon in Foxborough and drew a failing grade in the Post-Gazette's report card, and head coach Mike McCarthy has one week to sort it out before the Cincinnati Bengals visit Acrisure Stadium. The same report takes up cornerback Joey Porter Jr.'s contract situation as he sits out with a back injury.

sources.title: The Steelers are contemplating changes on the offensive line after Sunday's ugly showing

around_teams.title: Skenes Traces His Season Back to the Classic
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published an interview Monday, September 21, in which Pirates ace Paul Skenes discussed the struggles that marked his 2026 season and the part the World Baseball Classic played in them.
around_teams.summary: Skenes pitched in the tournament before reporting for the Pirates season, and he told the Post-Gazette how that schedule figured into the year that followed. The Pirates fell out of playoff contention September 19 and finish the season at PNC Park.

sources.title: Pirates ace Paul Skenes opens up about his struggles — and the role the World Baseball Classic played

around_teams.title: Four Steelers Answer for the Offense
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted a Press Pass session Sunday night, September 20, with tackle Troy Fautanu, linebacker Nick Herbig, receiver DK Metcalf, and tight end Pat Freiermuth taking questions after the Week 2 trip to Foxborough.
around_teams.summary: Metcalf spoke a day after adding two more drops to a rough start in Pittsburgh, and Fautanu answered for an offensive line the Post-Gazette graded as failing. Head coach Mike McCarthy had already told reporters the offense falls on him.

sources.title: Fautanu, Herbig, Metcalf, & Freiermuth on loss to Patriots | Press Pass | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: New Faces, Same Result at New England
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its Week 2 analysis Monday morning, September 21, concluding that the rebuilt Steelers offense produced the same frustration in Foxborough that the old one did.
around_teams.summary: Mike McCarthy took over play-calling this season with Aaron Rodgers at quarterback and DK Metcalf at receiver, and through two games the group has managed one touchdown. The Steelers host the Cincinnati Bengals next Sunday at Acrisure Stadium.

sources.title: Steelers Week 2 analysis: New faces, same frustrating result for the Steelers at New England

team_usa.title: Berhalter and Reyna Become the Veterans
team_usa.latest_developments: Sebastian Berhalter and Giovanni Reyna said Monday, September 21, that they have taken on leadership roles in Mauricio Pochettino's young United States squad, with Reyna, 23, saying the change "makes me feel a little bit old."
team_usa.summary: Pochettino left Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun out of this 28-player camp, the first of the 2030 World Cup cycle, and handed 16-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker Cavan Sullivan his first senior call-up. That leaves midfielders Berhalter and Reyna as the experienced hands through four coming friendlies.

sources.title: Berhalter, Reyna take on veteran roles for young USMNT squad
Sullivan, USMNT's gifted next generation kick-start road to 2030 World Cup

team_usa.title: Fredette Wins MVP in His First Tournament Back
team_usa.latest_developments: Jimmer Fredette took MVP honors at the FIBA 3x3 Phoenix Challenger on Sunday night, September 20, as Team Miami beat Amsterdam 22-16 for the title.
team_usa.summary: Fredette stepped down September 15 as managing director of USA Basketball's men's 3x3 program to end a two-year retirement and play again, with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in view. The Phoenix event was his first tournament since that return.

sources.title: Fredette wins MVP of 3x3 hoops tourney in return to court

team_usa.title: Downs Replaces the Injured Pepi
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Monday, September 21, that Damion Downs will take Ricardo Pepi's place on the United States men's national team roster for four coming friendlies.
team_usa.summary: PSV Eindhoven pulled Pepi off injured Sunday, September 20, costing manager Mauricio Pochettino a striker in the first camp of the 2030 World Cup cycle. Pochettino had already left Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun out of this 28-player squad.

sources.title: Downs replaces injured Ricardo Pepi for next four USMNT friendlies

team_usa.title: Mike Burton Dies at 79
team_usa.latest_developments: Mike Burton's son confirmed his father's death, ESPN reported Monday, September 21.
team_usa.summary: Burton won three Olympic swimming gold medals and became the first American to take the 1,500-meter freestyle at consecutive Games, in Mexico City in 1968 and Munich in 1972. He was 79.
